title: FancyZones sizing of Remote Desktop and VM connection windows
author: Scimitar21

status.label: Partial existing fix; split RDP and VM scenarios
status.detail: Open PR #51033 addresses the final Hyper-V VMConnect comment, not all original mstsc fullscreen/restore or remote-layout reports.

next_action.label: Validate each connection-window scenario separately
next_action.reason: Do not duplicate VMConnect work or assume it fixes the original RDP window-growth behavior.

judgment.rationale: The long discussion mixes local mstsc geometry, layouts inside remote sessions and Hyper-V guest resizing. Public steps already support reproduction, and new linked work covers only the last of these.
evidence: Original 0.29.3 report gives a local mstsc zone/fullscreen/restore sequence; the author later observed window growth even without PowerToys.
A commenter retested 0.47.0 after suggested merged PR #11776 and still observed growth; that PR only avoids zoning minimized windows.
The May 2024 discussion explicitly separates local RDP-window sizing from layouts inside remote sessions.
The final September 2024 comment concerns a Hyper-V Virtual Machine Connection guest not filling a 3837x1390 zone.
Open https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/51033 targets #51032 and that final VMConnect comment via drag-resize notifications, not the entire RDP discussion.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep VMConnect under #51032/#51033 and reproduce the original mstsc case independently with PowerToys on/off controls.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open PR #51033 is a concrete partial fix attempt for the Hyper-V VMConnect portion only. Original mstsc growth and remote-session layout persistence are not established as covered. Merged #11776 did not resolve the original symptom according to a subsequent test.

issue_context.summary: This issue combines local RDP client resizing, remote-session layout persistence and a later Hyper-V guest-size complaint. A new open PR addresses only the Hyper-V drag-snap scenario.
known_information: The original report includes Windows build, admin state and fullscreen/restore steps.
The author says RDP geometry also changes with PowerToys absent.
Later comments distinguish remote layout reset from the local window-growth symptom.
PR #51033 is open and describes a VMConnect-specific drag notification fix, with keyboard/non-drag snapping intentionally unchanged.
No current assignee or outstanding needs-author-feedback label exists.
inferences: Original RDP growth may be an external client/window-management issue, but a current controlled comparison is needed.
The VMConnect implementation cannot be assumed to fix unrelated mstsc or remote desktop layout behavior.
issue_context.analysis: Withdraw the generic request for steps and a fresh ZIP: the discussion already supplies concrete scenarios. A scoped maintainer test and explicit partial-fix accounting avoid both duplicate implementation and premature closure.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full report and all 25 comments, paginated timeline and related PR search.
Read #11776's merged scope and #51033's live open state, described resize ordering, affected WindowMouseSnap/WindowUtils/WorkArea files and stated validation limits.

actions.label: Separate mstsc restore from VMConnect guest sizing

reproduce.version: Current stable build; validate PR #51033 separately if a candidate is available
prerequisites: A reachable RDP host and classic mstsc client.
For the distinct VMConnect test, a Hyper-V enhanced-session guest and elevation needed to manipulate VMConnect.
Keep monitor/DPI and zone geometry fixed; record whether PowerToys runs locally or remotely.
steps: On the local PC, put mstsc into a zone, switch to fullscreen, restore down, and repeat while measuring the outer window rectangle.
Repeat the fullscreen/restore sequence with PowerToys fully exited to test the author's external-behavior observation.
Treat layouts inside the remote session as a separate test, not a pass/fail for the local mstsc window.
For VMConnect, Shift-drag the window into a zone and compare outer size with guest resolution.
Validate the VMConnect scenario against #51033 separately; do not infer that it fixes mstsc restore or remote-session layout persistence.
reproduce.expected_result: Original mstsc restore behavior is classified independently. The VMConnect candidate makes the guest follow a drag-snap resize within its stated scope.
